preference_alignment: Oral: YES (matches 'oral preferred'). Avoid severe myelosuppression veto: PARTIAL HIT — grade 3+ anemia ~29% sits on the named veto, no febrile-neutropenia signal. Avoid added neuropathy: not triggered.
guideline_status: NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 single-agent PARP maintenance, category 2A (all-comers after 1L platinum response).
rationale_summary: The critic and risktaker rank rucaparib as the second registered all-comer PARP that replicates the PRIMA signal in an independent phase 3 (ATHENA-MONO, n=538), with the benefit holding in the intent-to-treat population rather than resting on a BRCA-mutant stratum. That independent replication is what lifts it to the top of the unbranched ranking. The effect estimate is the ATHENA-MONO ITT HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.40-0.68) from the primary JCO publication (pmid:35658487). The same severe-myelosuppression veto that shadows niraparib applies here (grade 3+ anemia 28.7%), so it is no toxicity escape, only an evidence-quality near-tie with niraparib that the risktaker breaks toward niraparib on tumor-specific pharmacology.
open_questions: No tumor-partitioning or trapping pharmacology pointing rucaparib specifically at this BRCA-proficient biology, unlike niraparib
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate-to-high for PFS: replicated all-comer phase 3 (ATHENA-MONO ITT HR 0.52, 20.2 vs 9.2 mo) qualifying a BRCA-wild-type tumor without a BRCA or GIS gate.

counter_productive_moa.description: PARP myelosuppression is a patient-AE burden, not a mechanism that blunts the maintenance goal in genomically-unstable HGSC.

overall: Replicated all-comer PARP maintenance that qualifies a BRCA-wild-type tumor with no GIS gate; near-interchangeable with niraparib but lacks its tumor-specific pharmacology, and carries the same myelosuppression veto.

expected_benefit: PRIMA overall-population mPFS 13.8 vs 8.2 mo, HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.50-0.76, p<0.001); all-comer enrolment requires neither a BRCA mutation nor a validated HRD score.

Grade 3+ anemia 31%

preference_alignment: Oral: YES. Avoid severe myelosuppression veto: HIT — grade 3+ thrombocytopenia 28.7% / anemia 31% land squarely on the named veto; individualized starting dose blunts but does not erase it. Avoid added neuropathy: not triggered.
guideline_status: NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 single-agent PARP maintenance, category 2A (all-comers); ESMO endorses 1L PARP maintenance in this setting.
rationale_summary: Four of five personas (risktaker, conservative, critic, concensusite) call niraparib the cleanest efficacy and guideline fit: PRIMA is a registered, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 whose all-comer enrolment is the eligibility match itself for a BRCA-wild-type, genomically-unstable tumor — no cross-stratum extrapolation needed. The risktaker adds the only tumor-specific argument on the board: niraparib partitioned into tumor at 3.3x plasma and cut growth 58% in a BRCA-wild-type PDX where olaparib barely moved (pmid:30647846). It ranks below rucaparib only because of where the veto and dissent signal landed. The conservative issued a CONDITIONAL veto — against ranking niraparib at rank 1 on the patient's own myelosuppression veto — that it will withdraw once a hematology-supported, platelet-based starting-dose plan and a written cytopenia-management pathway are on file; the advocate dissented for the same reason, holding that the veto is the patient's to lift, not the board's to rank past on evidence. We override the veto to keep niraparib ranked and visible (per the no-silent-drop rule) but carry it at considered_with_caveats: the all-comer benefit is real and PFS-grade (OS immature, HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.44-1.11), and the larger HRD-positive effect (HR 0.43) does NOT apply without a validated score.
open_questions: Deliverability at this patient's marrow reserve (baseline WBC 3.5) is not established until a platelet-based starting-dose and cytopenia-management plan are documented
Whether the patient chooses to accept the myelosuppression risk with growth-factor/platelet support — the veto is hers to lift
likelihood_of_effect: High for PFS as an evidence fit: all-comer PRIMA phase 3 (HR 0.62, 13.8 vs 8.2 mo) plus BRCA-wild-type PDX pharmacology (pmid:30647846); deliverability gated by marrow reserve.

counter_productive_moa.description: Cytopenia-driven dose interruption on thin baseline marrow reserve can erode maintenance dose intensity; the advocate and conservative dissented on this toxicity-as-deliverability axis.

overall: Cleanest all-comer guideline and evidence fit with the only tumor-specific BRCA-wild-type pharmacology, but its grade 3+ thrombocytopenia/anemia hit the patient's named veto; deliverable only behind a documented hematology dose plan.

GI perforation / bowel-wall disruption 2.6%

preference_alignment: Avoid severe myelosuppression veto: CLEARED. Avoid added neuropathy: CLEARED. Modality caution 'thrombotic/bleeding risk': TENSION — anti-angiogenic VTE/bleeding risk presses the IVC-filter history, managed rather than escalated. Low-infusion-burden: PARTIAL (IV q3w, but she is already on it).
guideline_status: NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 bevacizumab maintenance, category 2A (all-comers after 1L platinum).
rationale_summary: The conservative and advocate lead with bevacizumab for the same patient-side reason: it is the only maintenance axis on the board that clears both named vetoes outright — no added neuropathy, no severe myelosuppression — on a backbone she already tolerates, with FDA approval since 2014 and more than a decade of post-marketing follow-up. The honest ceiling is PFS-only: GOG-218 and ICON7 show no overall-population OS benefit, and the critic insists it be labelled a PFS hold rather than a survival argument. The risktaker dissents on magnitude — leading with the smallest effect on the board (HR 0.717) for an efficacy-leaning (0.7) patient forfeits the larger PARP signal and banks the curve she is already riding. The operative caution is VTE/bleeding against her IVC-filter history, which the conservative and advocate both manage with established BP and bleeding monitoring rather than escalation.
open_questions: Whether continuing bevacizumab alone (vs layering a PARP once the GIS resolves) is the right maintenance intensity given the cleared Signatera MRD state
Magnitude in this stage IIIc R0 patient, who sits adjacent to but not inside ICON7's high-risk OS subset
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate for PFS only: GOG-218 HR 0.717 (14.1 vs 10.3 mo), RoB2-low but no overall-population OS gain; smallest maintenance effect on the board.
toxicity_burden: Low (grade 2+ hypertension 22.9%, GI-wall disruption 2.6%; VTE/bleeding class caution)

counter_productive_moa.description: Anti-angiogenic wound-healing and VTE/bleeding risk is a patient-AE caution here, not a mechanism that blunts maintenance benefit; risktaker dissent was magnitude/preference-flavored.

overall: The only maintenance that clears both named vetoes on a backbone she already tolerates, but PFS-only with no OS gain and a live VTE/bleeding caution against her IVC-filter history.

rationale_summary: The risktaker and advocate keep GEN-1 on the list as the continuation play: she is already on it and already at R0, and it works through the peritoneal immune microenvironment rather than the MSI/TMB checkpoint axis her MSS, TMB-low tumor forecloses, so the usual single-agent-ICI disqualifier does not apply. The OVATION 2 OS signal (HR 0.69) is large enough that the risktaker will not wave it off as a backbone afterthought. The honest weakness is maturity: efficacy rests on a sponsor topline and a 2025 abstract with CIs unreported and no peer-reviewed grade 3+ safety table, and the PFS magnitude trails the PARP options. rationale_summary: The conservative, concensusite, and advocate all keep letrozole as the gentlest option in front of the board — oral, once-daily, no infusion burden, and it trips none of her vetoes, which suits the 70-79 age band and her oral preference. Its agreement_score ties rucaparib's at 0.6 because nobody objected, but the evidence is the weakest on the list: pmid:29157627 is a non-randomized retrospective comparison nested in a translational ER-expression study (ROBINS-I serious, tier 4, n=80), and the critic insists the ROBINS-I Serious tag sit next to the rank so a reader does not take the 60% for a trial result. The clinician also flagged a design mismatch — the trials row described a single-arm phase 2, but the source is a retrospective translational series. PR-negativity predicts a more modest response than the ~80% ER reading alone suggests. It is the low-toxicity floor — a later-line or adjunct fallback, not a substitute for a randomized-backed maintenance regimen.
open_questions: Evidence is retrospective and non-randomized (ROBINS-I serious); no randomized letrozole-maintenance data in HGSC to anchor the estimate
Design-source mismatch flagged (single-arm phase 2 vs retrospective translational series) for screener reconciliation
PR-negativity magnitude — how much it tempers the ER-driven signal is unquantified
likelihood_of_effect: Low and weakly evidenced: only a retrospective ROBINS-I-serious series (60% vs 38.5% RFS at 24 mo, pmid:29157627); PR-negativity tempers the ER-driven signal.
toxicity_burden: Low (arthralgia, bone-density loss on prolonged aromatase inhibition; no named veto triggered)

counter_productive_moa.description: Endocrine blockade has no plausible counter-productive vector in ER-positive HGSC; the dissent here is evidence-quality, not mechanism.

overall: The lowest-toxicity oral option that clears every veto and fits the age band, but the evidence is a single retrospective ROBINS-I-serious series and PR-negativity tempers the expected magnitude.

intervention_label: Olaparib + bevacizumab (PAOLA-1 maintenance, contingent on validated HRD-positive)
expected_benefit: PAOLA-1 HRD-positive subgroup mPFS 37.2 vs 17.7 mo, HR 0.33 (95% CI 0.25-0.45); BRCA-non-mutated HRD-positive subgroup HR 0.43. Pre-specified ITT was HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.49-0.72), mPFS 22.1 vs 16.6 mo — the load-bearing 0.33 is a subgroup, not the ITT, estimate.
key_risks: Combination-arm grade 3+ AE ~57%
Grade 3+ hypertension 19% — compounds the VTE/bleeding caution against her IVC-filter history
Grade 3+ anemia 17% (PARP myelosuppression veto)
Up to 20% discontinued olaparib for AEs
preference_alignment: Stacks two of her concerns at once: PARP myelosuppression veto HIT (grade 3+ anemia 17%) AND bevacizumab thrombotic/bleeding caution against the IVC-filter history. Oral olaparib half: YES; IV bevacizumab half: she is already on it.
guideline_status: NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 category 1 — but ONLY for HRD-positive disease defined by tumor BRCA or a validated GIS >=42, which this BRCA-wild-type tumor does not yet meet.
rationale_summary: This is the highest-magnitude maintenance on the board (HRD-positive HR 0.33), and the patient is already on the bevacizumab half — but it ranks last and carries a double veto for two distinct, both-live reasons. The conservative vetoed it on toxicity: combination-arm grade 3+ AE near 57% with grade 3+ hypertension 19%, stacked onto a patient with high VTE history and a prior IVC filter, with no compensating mitigation evidence in the record; that veto lifts only with a documented anticoagulation/BP plan AND a confirmed GIS >=42. The critic vetoed it on evidence quality: the load-bearing HR 0.33 is a pre-specified subgroup, the ITT was a materially smaller HR 0.59, and the patient has no validated GIS, so she does not even clear the companion-diagnostic gate that defines the subgroup. We keep the row visible (no silent drop) at considered_with_caveats because the risktaker, concensusite, and advocate all hold it as a CONTINGENT high-upside option: if a Myriad MyChoice CDx GIS returns >=42 the eligibility gate opens, both vetoes become addressable, and this regimen reorders upward. Below 42 she is HRD-negative and this option is foreclosed. The GIS itself is surfaced under Workup considerations, not as a ranked row, because every biomarker has now resulted.
open_questions: Eligibility is gated on a validated MyChoice CDx GIS >=42 the patient does not yet have; Altera's qualitative instability call does not satisfy the companion-diagnostic definition
Whether a documented anticoagulation/BP-management plan can be assembled to lift the conservative's toxicity veto given the IVC-filter history
The load-bearing effect is a subgroup, not ITT, estimate — the ITT HR 0.59 is the conservative read until GIS confirms HRD-positive
likelihood_of_effect: High ONLY if GIS >=42 confirms HRD-positive: PAOLA-1 subgroup HR 0.33 (37.2 vs 17.7 mo); contingent and foreclosed below 42, ITT effect is a smaller HR 0.59.
toxicity_burden: High (combination grade 3+ AE ~57%; hypertension 19%, anemia 17%, up to 20% olaparib discontinuation)

counter_productive_moa.description: Anti-angiogenic VTE/bleeding load stacked on PARP myelosuppression against an IVC-filter history; two vetoes stood on toxicity and evidence-quality grounds.

overall: Highest-magnitude maintenance if HRD-positive is confirmed, but contingent on a GIS she lacks and double-vetoed on stacked VTE/myelosuppression toxicity and a subgroup-only effect estimate.
